page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top left, page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: ni sint quibus efficacia illa erroris mittatur; verum, quia cum ejusmodi Homines ii sint, qui Veritati non obediunt, ut ibidem Paulus ait; ii vero, qui veritati non obedient, aut pessimi quidam & perversi sunt Homines, aut ejusmodi qui nimis negligentes in Rebus divinis sunt, quorum semper ingens fuit, & futurus est Numerus; certum est, non defuturos unquam, qui ea Punitione Dei sint digni.

§. 62. Hæc Socinus. At Inter illius Discipulos, nemo audacius Naturæ divinæ Perfectiones violavit, tum subtrahendo quæ ei debita erant, tum affingendo quæ ei maxime incongrua erant, & eo profusius indigna, quàm Conradus Vorstius, Professor olim Theologiæ in Academia Leidensi, cujus libros proinde, qui blasphema ista Dogmata continebant, Seren. Rex noster Jacobus publice cremari jussit in Cæmeterio Paulino & in utraque Academia. Intercessit quoque, per legatum suum, cum fœderatis Belgii Ordinibus, ut Illum, non solum Munere professorio privarent, sed etiam è finibus suæ ditionis pellerent. Et, ut palam ostenderet, quanto zelo tueretur fidem antiquam & Apostolicam, cujus ipse defensor erat, contra insana & impia Vorstii Dogmata, edidit libellum, cui Titulum dedit, Protestatio Antivorstia, in quo Illorum præcipua & maxime perniciosa notavit, excerpta è variis Ipsius Tractatibus, quorum Titulos & paginas in margine citat. Hæc autem fere sunt. Nihil vetat Deo etiam Corpus ascribere, si vocabulum Corporis in Significatione latiore sumamus. Non satis circumspecte loquuntur, qui Deum, ut essentia, sic etiam voluntate, prorsus immutabilem esse affirmant. page.notes: Top four lines are italic and continue the paragraph from the previous page. The paragraph "§. 62." is set in roman with italic passages marked as printed; the italic run at the end of the page is marked as italic from "Nihil vetat" onward. The line "ni sint" is partly blurred, with "sint" read from context and [?] not added because the letters are legible. "De fana" in the running head is blurred; the first letter is uncertain. The final word is split as "ha-" at the line end, with "bere" as catchword. Several words in the middle of the page are smeared by print show-through and low contrast ("mittatur", "obedient", "Discipulos"); these are transcribed as best read. "Vorstii" and "Vorstius" are printed with long s rendered as s.
